# RNA-Seq Data Download Quick Reference

## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1. Get SRR accessions from GEO

```{bash}
# Option A: Using the comprehensive script
./download_data.sh geo-to-srr -g GSE280953

# Option B: Using E-utilities directly
esearch -db gds -query "GSE280953" | \
  elink -target sra | \
  efetch -format runinfo | \
  tail -n +2 | cut -d',' -f1 > SRR_list.txt
```

### 2. Choose your download method

**For fast, reliable connections:**

```{bash}
./download_data.sh sra-parallel -i SRR_list.txt -t 16
```

**For unstable connections:**

```{bash}
./download_data.sh sra-prefetch -i SRR_list.txt -t 8
```

**Fastest overall (ENA):**

```{bash}
./download_data.sh ena -i SRR_list.txt
```

---

## 📊 Comparison of Methods

| Method | Speed | Reliability | Best For | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------------|----------|-------|
| **parallel-fastq-dump** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐ | Multiple files | Fastest for batch downloads |
| **fasterq-dump** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐ | Single files | Good balance |
| **prefetch + fasterq-dump** | ⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Unstable connections | Most robust |
| **ENA** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | International users | Often faster than NCBI |
| **aspera** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Large files | Requires setup |

## 🛠️ Installation Commands

### SRA Toolkit

```{bash}
# Using conda (recommended)
conda install -c bioconda sra-tools

# Verify installation
fastq-dump --version
fasterq-dump --version
prefetch --version
```

### parallel-fastq-dump

```{bash}
pip install parallel-fastq-dump

# Verify
parallel-fastq-dump --version
```

### NCBI Datasets

```{bash}
conda install -c conda-forge ncbi-datasets-cli

# Verify
datasets --version
```

### NCBI E-utilities

```{bash}
conda install -c bioconda entrez-direct

# Verify
esearch -version
```

### GNU Parallel (for batch processing)

```{bash}
# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install parallel

# macOS
brew install parallel

# Conda
conda install -c conda-forge parallel
```

## 💡 Common Use Cases

### Case 1: Download entire GEO dataset

```{bash}
# Step 1: Get SRR list
./download_data.sh geo-to-srr -g GSE280953

# Step 2: Download all files
./download_data.sh sra-parallel -i SRR_list.txt -t 16 -o my_project/data

# Step 3: Verify downloads
./post_download_qc.sh my_project/data/fastq
```

### Case 2: Resume interrupted download

```{bash}
# Use the tracker script
./download_tracker.sh SRR_list.txt downloads/fastq

# This creates:
# - completed_downloads.txt (successful)
# - failed_downloads.txt (failed)

# The script automatically skips completed files
```

### Case 3: Download with disk space monitoring

```{bash}
# Terminal 1: Start disk monitor
./disk_monitor.sh downloads/fastq &

# Terminal 2: Start downloads
./download_tracker.sh SRR_list.txt downloads/fastq
```


### Case 4: Parallel download with resource limits

```{bash}
# Download 4 files simultaneously, 8 threads each
TOTAL_CORES=32
JOBS=4
THREADS_PER_JOB=8

cat SRR_list.txt | parallel -j $JOBS \
  fasterq-dump {} \
    --outdir downloads/fastq \
    --threads $THREADS_PER_JOB \
    --split-files \
    --progress

# Compress in parallel
find downloads/fastq -name "*.fastq" | parallel -j $TOTAL_CORES gzip {}
```


### Case 5: Download from ENA with verification

```{bash}
# Download and verify checksums
./download_verify.sh SRR12345678 downloads/fastq

# Check for failures
cat checksum_failures.txt
```

## 🔧 Troubleshooting

### Problem: "Network error" or timeout
**Solution:**

```{bash}
# Use prefetch method (more robust)
./download_data.sh sra-prefetch -i SRR_list.txt

# Or try ENA instead
./download_data.sh ena -i SRR_list.txt
```


### Problem: "Out of disk space"
**Solution:**

```{bash}
# Monitor space before starting
df -h

# Delete SRA cache (after conversion to FASTQ)
rm -rf ~/ncbi/public/sra/*

# Or download only what you need
head -5 SRR_list.txt > subset.txt
./download_data.sh sra-fast -i subset.txt
```


### Problem: Corrupted files
**Solution:**

```{bash}
# Check file integrity
gzip -t downloads/fastq/*.fastq.gz

# Re-download failed files
grep "FAILED" download.log | awk '{print $2}' > failed.txt
./download_data.sh sra-fast -i failed.txt
```


### Problem: Slow download speed
**Solution:**

```{bash}
# Try ENA (often faster)
./download_data.sh ena -i SRR_list.txt

# Or use aspera (if available)
ascp -QT -l 300m -P33001 \
  -i ~/.aspera/connect/etc/asperaweb_id_dsa.openssh \
  era-fasp@fasp.sra.ebi.ac.uk:/vol1/fastq/SRR123/SRR12345678_1.fastq.gz .
```

### Problem: "SRA accession not found"
**Solution:**

```{bash}
# Verify accession exists
esearch -db sra -query "SRR12345678" | efetch -format docsum

# Check if it's an ENA-only accession
# Try downloading from ENA instead
```

## 📁 File Organization

Recommended directory structure:

```{bash}
project/
├── raw_data/
│   ├── fastq/              # Downloaded FASTQ files
│   ├── metadata/           # GEO metadata, sample info
│   └── logs/               # Download logs
├── processed/
│   ├── aligned/            # BAM files
│   ├── counts/             # Count matrices
│   └── qc/                 # QC reports
├── results/
│   ├── deseq2/             # DESeq2 results
│   └── enrichment/         # GO enrichment
└── scripts/                # Analysis scripts
```

---

## ⚡ Performance Tips

1. **Use SSD for downloads** - Much faster I/O
2. **Compress immediately** - Save disk space
3. **Use parallel downloads** - But don't overload the network
4. **Clean up temp files** - SRA toolkit creates large temp files
5. **Use local cache** - Configure SRA toolkit cache location

### Configure SRA Toolkit

```{bash}
# Set cache location
vdb-config --interactive

# Or edit config file directly
mkdir -p ~/.ncbi
cat > ~/.ncbi/user-settings.mkfg << EOF
/repository/user/main/public/root = "/path/to/large/disk"
EOF
```

---

## 🔍 Verification Checklist

After downloading, verify:
- [ ] All files downloaded (compare with SRR_list.txt)
- [ ] No empty files (`find . -size 0`)
- [ ] No corrupted gzip files (`gzip -t *.fastq.gz`)
- [ ] Paired-end files exist in pairs (R1 and R2)
- [ ] File sizes reasonable (>100MB for typical RNA-seq)
- [ ] Check first few reads (`zcat file.fastq.gz | head -n 20`)

## 🎯 Best Practice Workflow

```{bash}
# 1. Get accessions
./download_data.sh geo-to-srr -g GSE280953

# 2. Test with one sample first
head -1 SRR_list.txt > test.txt
./download_data.sh sra-fast -i test.txt

# 3. If successful, download all
./download_tracker.sh SRR_list.txt downloads/fastq

# 4. Quality check
./post_download_qc.sh downloads/fastq

# 5. Proceed with analysis
# (alignment, quantification, etc.)
```
